scope.attribution: Native time includes all native work and client reply parsing. No separate parser, file-check or import-resolution timers exist; their individual costs cannot be inferred. Native calls count process starts, including find and inputs-only.
scope.bytes: Canonical JSON reply bytes, not exact wire bytes. Store reads and offered writes count repeated object operations. Added bytes count unique object files; offered writes can verify existing objects. Manifest pointer bytes are outside object totals but their I/O is timed. Temporary native reuse files are timed but not retained in the object inventory.
scope.claims: Disclosed synthetic development examples only. No unfamiliar package, agent task, paid study, full-package acceptance or general speedup claim.
scope.elapsed_seconds: Parent timer around a new Python worker through parsed JSON reply. Includes Python/SDK startup, finding the function, native process startup, file checks, import resolution, parsing, analysis or validation, saved-record reads/writes and manifest pointer I/O.
scope.excluded: Checkout, compilation, dependency installation, fixture edits, ordinary Python observation, store inventory, report comparison and audit. Worker reply serialization/transfer, shared measurement imports and instrumentation are included. Native project caching is explicitly disabled for every call. OS file caches are neither flushed nor controlled.
scope.memory: Separate worker and largest-child lifetime RSS high-water marks, not sampled aggregate RSS. Python runtime and fr are separate processes.
scope.python: Ordinary Python executes the same selected function with source returning 17 and sink returning its argument. It checks one concrete result, not all input-flow paths. Its elapsed time is contextual, not an equivalent analysis baseline.
